approach-per-package-job-model.reason: A per-package job model makes branch protection grow by hand for every package and produces exactly the silent degradation F1 identifies: the job runs, it is not required, and a red one cannot block a merge. Its context names also move as packages are added, and the CodeScene App evidence proves a renamed context silently stops being the thing that was pinned, so per-package names cannot serve as gates.

Packages sit under three different roots, so a single filesystem glob cannot discover them and only a declared list with an assertion is both explicit and complete.
approach-explicit-list-unasserted.reason: The unasserted list does not remove the silent-coverage failure; it relocates it. A package added without a list entry is uncovered and nothing fails, which is the likelier failure mode because nothing forces the list edit. The completeness assertion makes the enumeration fail closed in both directions, which is the repository's existing idiom (check-coherence.mjs pins counts; check-scope.mjs classifies every path) rather than a new invention.

forces: An explicit package list has its own silent-failure mode: a package added without a list entry is uncovered and nothing fails, so the list must be provably complete.
Packages sit under three different roots, so a single filesystem glob cannot discover them and only a declared list with an assertion is both explicit and complete.
approach-filesystem-discovery.reason: The packages sit under three different roots (contracts/, packages/, research/), so no single glob can discover them, which independently rules out pure filesystem discovery. Glob discovery also makes coverage silent in the other direction: a scanned directory that misses a root yields a quietly uncovered package, exactly the failure the completeness assertion is designed to surface.

approach-repository-wide-node-matrix.reason: A repository-wide matrix has no third option: it must run the contract below its declared >=26.5.0 range or drop Node 24 from the SDK's >=24 <25 || >=26 <27 range. Both outcomes violate a declared engine range, and the per-package matrix preserves each package's recorded range without reconciliation.

gh pr checks --required lists only contexts that have reported, so merge gates must count against branch protection's declared context list, never the reported set.
approach-skip-shaped-as-pass.reason: A pass-shaped skip produces a green board that has verified nothing, which is the #191 defect class and the single most dangerous failure mode in the recorded decision. Counting merge readiness from the reported set compounds it: gh pr checks --required lists only contexts that have reported, so a check that never started is invisible there and a declared required context can silently drop out.
